pashtofolksong.sound: The village and hujra song of the Pashtuns of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and eastern and southern Afghanistan: two-line tappa verses and fast, chorus-answered charbeta epics, sung over rubab, harmonium, mangai pot drum or tabla and dhol.
markers: Short two-line tappa verses, the second line longer than the first
Bright rubab runs over a driving pot-drum or dhol beat
In charbeta, a fast lead line answered by a chorus
near: A Coke Studio fusion arrangement of a Zarsanga folk song with a band and a pop singer: the song is folk, the record is studio pop
Rubab-and-guitar band cover of a classic folk song made for Coke Studio, a modern fusion rather than the village or radio folk style
Pashtu - Come To Me In The Morning (Kabuli Style)
Kabul radio star singing in the urban Kabuli style with harmonium and rubab: Afghan radio light song rather than tappa or charbeta

bhawaiyaandbhatial.sound: Folk song of the Bengal countryside in two strands: bhawaiya from Rangpur, Cooch Behar and Goalpara, sung over the two-string dotara about cart drivers, buffalo herders and women left waiting, and bhatiali, the boatmen's song of the river delta, sung freely in long, high, drawn-out lines.
markers: Long, drawn-out melancholy vocal lines
Two-string dotara accompaniment
Bouncy, skipping chatka songs alongside the slow ones
near: Hindi film song from Bandini: S. D. Burman borrows the bhatiali melody, but it is an orchestrated studio film song, not a folk song
Raag Khamaj (Pahadi Dhun) & Folk Music of Bengal & Assam: Bhatiali & Bihu
A sarod recital that quotes bhatiali and bihu tunes inside a raga performance; instrumental art music, not the sung folk form

hsaingwaing.window: 1600 onward (first pictured in the 1600s; recorded from the 1950s)
hsaingwaing.sound: Burma's loud outdoor ensemble for theatre, puppet plays, Buddhist ceremonies and spirit rites: a leader seated inside a ring of 21 tuned drums plays the tune with a gong circle, gong chime and a nasal hne oboe, all in heterophony over bell and clapper.
markers: A circle of tuned drums carrying the melody in fast virtuoso runs
Bronze gong circle and a shrill double-reed oboe doubling the tune
Sudden lurches in tempo and rhythm, held together by a small bell and clapper
fits: Hsaing waing orchestra of Master Sein Tin Htay
Pat Waing: The Magic Drum Circle of Burma (album)
near: Inle Myint Maung & Yi Yi Thant
In Praise Of The Burmese Harp
Classical song with the arched saung harp: an intimate indoor chamber piece, no drum circle, gongs or oboe
Thai piphat: the same family of gong circles and oboe, but xylophones and barrel drums lead and there is no tuned drum circle

zapinandjoget.window: zapin from about the 14th century, joget from the colonial era in Malacca (recorded from 1931)
zapinandjoget.sound: Malay social-dance music of the Straits: zapin pairs the gambus lute and interlocking marwas frame drums with sung pantun verses, often opened by a free gambus solo; joget is quicker, a violin over gong and rebana with a teasing lilt that plays twos against threes.
markers: Gambus lute leading, often opening with a free, unmetered solo
Interlocking marwas frame drums driving the zapin beat between sung verses
A quick joget violin over gong and rebana, beats felt in twos and threes at once
fits: Kumpulan Asli Kuala Lumpur, conducted by Fadzil Ahmad
Kumpulan Asli Kuala Lumpur, conducted by Fadzil Ahmad
Orkès Gambus Al-Hidayah with Fahmi Alwialhadi
Melayu Music of Sumatra and the Riau Islands (album)
near: Soneta Group (Rhoma Irama and Elvy Sukaesih)
Named after the dance, but a dangdut record by the founders of dangdut, not Malay dance-orchestra music
A zapin song recast on a dangdut beat; catalogued as dangdut and ethno-pop
Prize-winning creative ethnic pop (irama Malaysia) from the same singers, a pop fusion rather than a zapin or joget dance tune
Sits on the same album as her zapin and joget but is a keroncong song

maracatu.window: c. 1700 onward (first written record 1711; recorded on album from the 1990s)
maracatu.sound: Afro-Brazilian carnival processional music of Pernambuco: massed rope-tuned alfaia bass drums, snares and a gonguê bell under call-and-response songs (loas) in the urban baque virado of Recife and Olinda nations, and a faster, brass-led baque solto in the rural Mata Norte form.
markers: A wall of heavy alfaia bass drums playing interlocking, syncopated patterns
A clanging gonguê bell and rattling abê shakers riding over the drums
A solo singer answered by a chorus in short, repeated loas
fits: Maracatu Nação Estrela Brilhante Do Recife (album)
near: Maracatu drums fused with rock guitar, funk and hip-hop vocals: a band song, not a nação's processional loa
Recife carnival too, but a breakneck brass march led by horns, with no alfaia drum corps or call-and-response loa

currulao.window: c. 1700 onward (recorded from at least the 1970s)
currulao.sound: Afro-descendant marimba music of the southern Pacific coast of Colombia and Esmeraldas in Ecuador: a chonta-wood marimba over bamboo resonators leads two bombo bass drums, two cununo hand drums and guasá shakers, while women cantadoras answer a lead voice in rough three-part harmony.
markers: A wooden chonta marimba with a low ostinato and a high improvising part
Deep bombos and slapped cununos in a rolling 6/8
Call-and-response between a lead singer and a chorus of women shaking guasás
near: Big-band salsa from Cali with brass, piano and congas: Pacific-born musicians, but no marimba, bombos or cantadora chorus

jota.window: c. 1700 onward (named from the 18th century; recorded on 78s from the early 20th century, in the field by Alan Lomax in 1952, revived by folk groups from the 1970s)
jota.sound: Spain's most widespread folk song and dance, strongest in Aragon: a fast triple-time dance played by a rondalla of bandurrias, lutes and guitars with castanets, framing a slow, ornamented solo verse sung at full voice; other regions play it on dulzaina and drum, bagpipes or tambourines.
markers: Brisk 3/4 or 3/8 lilt in a major key, swinging between tonic and dominant seventh
Bandurria and lute melody over strummed guitars and clicking castanets
A powerful solo voice slowing down for an ornamented eight-syllable quatrain
near: A Russian composer's 1845 concert overture built on the Aragonese jota tune: full orchestra, no singer, rondalla or dancers
A jota written for the zarzuela stage and sung by an operatic tenor with orchestra, not a cantador with a rondalla

hardangerfiddleand.window: c. 1700 onward (the oldest surviving Hardanger fiddle is from 1651; recorded on 78s by the 1920s)
hardangerfiddleand.sound: Solo fiddle dance music of southern and western Norway played on the Hardanger fiddle, whose sympathetic understrings ring under constant double-stopping, in local tunings, for the bygdedans: gangar, springar and the acrobatic halling, plus listening pieces (lydarslåttar) and bridal marches.
markers: Shimmering drone from sympathetic strings under two-string bowing
Springar in an uneven three-beat pulse that differs from valley to valley
Fiddler's foot stamping the beat, solo and unaccompanied
fits: Torleiv H. Bjørgum and Hallvard T. Bjørgum
near: Grieg's piano settings of Hardanger tunes noted down from the fiddler Knut Dahle: concert piano music, no fiddle, drone or dance pulse
Hardanger fiddle on ECM, but his own composed and improvised solo music, not traditional slåttar for dancing
